title: UrbanThread Apparel opens 220,000 sq ft fulfilment centre and plans sortation automation
body: UrbanThread Apparel has opened a 220,000 sq ft fulfilment centre in Hoskote to handle rising online orders, which have grown to 60,000 a day. The D2C fashion brand said it will add automated sortation and a pick-to-light system within six months, and it is replacing its current warehouse management system with one that can manage returns and multi-warehouse inventory. UrbanThread expects to finalise technology partners before the year-end sale season. The brand said returns account for about a fifth of its online orders, and that faster processing of returned items is one of the main goals of the new fulfilment centre.

title: MoveLinx 3PL adds 1.5 million sq ft of warehousing and new client contracts
body: MoveLinx 3PL will add 1.5 million sq ft of warehousing across Chennai, Pune and Kolkata over the next 12 months after signing contracts with two consumer electronics brands and a pharmaceutical distributor. The company said it plans to automate the new sites with shuttle systems and autonomous mobile robots, and it is standardising on one warehouse management system and transport management system across its network. MoveLinx operates about 9 million sq ft of warehousing across 40 cities, and said customers increasingly want real-time inventory visibility and faster order turnaround from their 3PL.

title: Kaveri Gateway Ports awarded concession for new container berth and yard automation
body: Kaveri Gateway Ports has been awarded a 30-year concession to build and operate a new container berth with a capacity of 800,000 TEU a year. The INR 3,400 crore project includes a new automated yard, a gate automation system and a reefer area with 1,200 plug points. The port operator said it will issue tenders for a terminal operating system, yard cranes and reefer monitoring in the next quarter. The port handled about 520,000 TEU last year, and the operator said shipping lines have asked for faster truck turnaround and more reefer capacity for agricultural and seafood exports.

title: Frostline Cold Logistics raises funding to build three pharma cold chain hubs
body: Frostline Cold Logistics has raised INR 350 crore from an infrastructure fund to build three temperature-controlled hubs for pharmaceuticals and vaccines in Ahmedabad, Hyderabad and Guwahati. The hubs will have a combined 60,000 pallet positions across frozen, chilled and ambient zones. Frostline said it will invest in real-time temperature monitoring for its 400 reefer trucks and a warehouse management system that supports batch and expiry tracking. Frostline currently operates 18 cold storage facilities, and said demand from vaccine makers and specialty drug distributors has grown sharply since new storage guidelines were introduced.

title: Dhanvi Beauty raises Series B and plans automated warehouse to ship 40,000 orders a day
body: D2C beauty brand Dhanvi Beauty has raised USD 38 million in a Series B round and will build an automated warehouse near Gurugram capable of shipping 40,000 orders a day. The brand currently relies on two third-party warehouses and wants more control over fulfilment speed and returns. Dhanvi said it is evaluating goods-to-person automation, a new WMS and a multi-carrier shipping platform. Dhanvi sells more than 300 skincare and makeup products online and through 2,000 retail doors, and said its order volumes have tripled over the last eighteen months.

title: Mahanagar Mart to open two regional distribution centres to serve 400 new stores
body: Supermarket chain Mahanagar Mart will open two regional distribution centres in Nagpur and Indore, totalling 700,000 sq ft, to supply 400 new stores planned over three years. The retailer said the centres will have separate chilled and frozen zones for fresh produce and dairy. Mahanagar is looking for warehouse automation, a transport management system for store replenishment and cold chain monitoring for its delivery fleet. Mahanagar operates 260 stores across Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, and said fresh produce wastage and store stock-outs are the main problems it wants the new centres to address.

title: Parkline Industrial Parks launches 2.4 million sq ft logistics park near Chennai
body: Parkline Industrial Parks has launched a 2.4 million sq ft grade-A logistics park at Oragadam near Chennai, with the first 800,000 sq ft ready for tenants in March. The developer said it has signed letters of intent with a 3PL and two e-commerce companies. Parkline plans to offer built-to-suit fulfilment centres with pre-installed automation and is in talks with automation vendors to create a standard offering for tenants. The developer said demand for grade-A warehousing in Chennai has grown strongly as manufacturers and online retailers expand in the region, keeping vacancy rates in single digits.

title: Kargoline Express invests in 12 new sortation hubs as parcel volumes surge
body: Express parcel company Kargoline Express will invest INR 900 crore in 12 new sortation hubs across tier-two cities over the next 18 months as e-commerce parcel volumes grow ahead of the festive season. Each hub will handle up to 300,000 parcels a day. Kargoline said the hubs will use cross-belt sorters and dimensioning systems, and it is upgrading its transport management system for line-haul planning. Kargoline delivered about 480 million parcels last year and said volumes from tier-two and tier-three cities are growing faster than from the large metros for the third year running.

title: Himsagar Seafoods builds export cold storage at Visakhapatnam port
body: Himsagar Seafoods will build a 25,000-tonne export cold storage facility near Visakhapatnam port to support rising shrimp exports to the United States and Europe. The INR 180 crore project includes blast freezers, a packing unit and a dedicated reefer truck fleet. Himsagar said it needs temperature logging that meets importer audit requirements, and it is evaluating cold chain monitoring and warehouse management systems. Himsagar exported about 18,000 tonnes of frozen shrimp last year, and said overseas buyers are increasingly demanding complete temperature records from farm to port for every shipment.

title: Sattvik Foods opens new snacks plant and automated distribution centre in Indore
body: Packaged foods company Sattvik Foods has opened a new snacks plant and an adjacent 250,000 sq ft distribution centre in Indore, with an investment of INR 480 crore. The company said the distribution centre will serve modern trade, quick-commerce and 35 super-stockists across central India. Sattvik is adding automated storage and retrieval, and a transport management system to plan deliveries from the new site. Sattvik said sales through quick-commerce platforms have doubled in the last year, and that faster replenishment from the new centre should reduce stock-outs in its fastest-selling products.

title: Bayshore Rail Logistics opens inland container depot with 400,000 TEU capacity
body: Bayshore Rail Logistics has opened an inland container depot near Ludhiana with a capacity of 400,000 TEU a year, connected to western ports by dedicated freight corridor. The depot includes a 150,000 sq ft bonded warehouse and a cold chain facility for agricultural exports. Bayshore said it is deploying a terminal operating system and yard management tools and will add warehouse automation to the bonded facility next year. The company said exporters in Punjab currently truck containers more than 1,000 kilometres to the ports, and the rail link is expected to cut transit times and costs significantly.

title: SwiftCrate raises USD 75 million to add 200 dark stores and a mother warehouse
body: Quick-commerce start-up SwiftCrate has raised USD 75 million in a Series C round to open 200 dark stores and a 300,000 sq ft mother warehouse in Mumbai. The company delivers groceries in under 15 minutes in six cities. SwiftCrate said it will invest in a warehouse management system that can handle dark store replenishment, cold chain monitoring for dairy and frozen goods, and route planning for its rider fleet. SwiftCrate said average order values have grown by a third this year and that fresh and frozen categories now make up about 40 per cent of the orders it delivers every day.
